593class Rectangle2(Rectangle):
594    """A rectangle defined by two opposite corners.
595
596    Examples:
597        >>> rect = Rectangle2((0, 0), (40, 80))
598        >>> rect.width
599        40.0
600        >>> rect.height
601        80.0
602    """
603
604    def __init__(
605        self, corner1: PointType, corner2: PointType, **kwargs: object
606    ) -> None:
607        """Initialize a ``Rectangle2`` from two opposite corners.
608
609        Args:
610            corner1 (PointType): The first corner of the rectangle.
611            corner2 (PointType): The second corner of the rectangle.
612            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments.
613        """
614        x1, y1 = corner1[:2]
615        x2, y2 = corner2[:2]
616        x_min, x_max = min(x1, x2), max(x1, x2)
617        y_min, y_max = min(y1, y2), max(y1, y2)
618        center = ((x_min + x_max) / 2, (y_min + y_max) / 2)
619        width = x_max - x_min
620        height = y_max - y_min
621        super().__init__(width, height, center, **kwargs)
622
623    def __repr__(self) -> str:
624        """Return a Rectangle string from this rectangle's vertices.
625
626        The subtype is ``RECTANGLE``, so the name is Rectangle.
627
628        Examples:
629            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
630            >>> repr(sg.Rectangle2((0, 0), (40, 80)))
631            'Rectangle([(0.0, 0.0), ..., (0.0, 80.0)])'
632            >>> str(sg.Rectangle2((0, 0), (40, 80))).startswith("Shape")
633            True
634        """
635        if len(self.primary_points) == 0:
636            return "Rectangle()"
637        if len(self.primary_points) < 4:
638            return f"Rectangle({self.vertices})"
639        return f"Rectangle([{self.vertices[0]}, ..., {self.vertices[-1]}])"

class Circle(simetri.shapes.shape.Shape): 
642class Circle(Shape):
643    """Circle defined by radius and optional center.
644
645    Stored as a one-point shape at the center; ``radius`` drives drawing and
646    the bounding box.
647
648    Attributes:
649        center: Center point (alias for the single vertex).
650        radius: Circle radius.
651        subtype: Always ``Types.CIRCLE``.
652
653    Examples:
654        >>> c = sg.Circle(radius=40, center=(20, 20))
655        >>> tuple(float(x) for x in c.center[:2])
656        (20.0, 20.0)
657    """
658
659    def __init__(
660        self,
661        radius: float | None = None,
662        center: PointType = (0, 0),
663        xform_matrix: np.ndarray | None = None,
664        **kwargs: object,
665    ) -> None:
666        """Initialize a Circle.
667
668        Args:
669            radius: Circle radius. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["circle_radius"]``.
670            center: Center point. Defaults to ``(0, 0)``.
671            xform_matrix: Optional initial transform.
672            **kwargs: Additional shape keyword arguments.
673        """
674        if radius is None:
675            radius = runtime_defaults["circle_radius"]
676
677        x, y = center[:2]
678        points = [[x, y]]
679        super().__init__(points, xform_matrix=xform_matrix, **kwargs)
680        self.subtype = Types.CIRCLE
681        self._radius = radius
682
683    def __repr__(self) -> str:
684        """Return a Circle string from this circle's vertices.
685
686        Examples:
687            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
688            >>> repr(sg.Circle(radius=40, center=(20, 20)))
689            'Circle(((20.0, 20.0),))'
690            >>> str(sg.Circle(radius=40, center=(20, 20)))
691            'Shape(((20.0, 20.0),))'
692        """
693        if len(self.primary_points) == 0:
694            return "Circle()"
695        if len(self.primary_points) < 4:
696            return f"Circle({self.vertices})"
697        return f"Circle([{self.vertices[0]}, ..., {self.vertices[-1]}])"
698
699    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: object) -> None:
700        """Set an attribute of the circle.
701
702        Args:
703            name (str): The name of the attribute.
704            value (Any): The value of the attribute.
705        """
706        if name == "center":
707            self[0] = value[:2]
708        elif name == "radius":
709            ratio = value / self.radius
710            self.scale(ratio, about=self.center, reps=0)
711        else:
712            super().__setattr__(name, value)
713
714    @property
715    def b_box(self) -> BoundingBox:
716        """Return the axis-aligned bounding box of the circle.
717
718        Under an affine transform the circle becomes an ellipse. Half-widths
719        are ``_radius`` times the Euclidean norms of the linear matrix rows,
720        so non-uniform scale and shear are handled correctly.
721
722        Returns:
723            BoundingBox: The bounding box of the shape.
724        """
725        x, y = self.center[:2]
726        linear = self.xform_matrix[:2, :2]
727        half_width = self._radius * float(np.linalg.norm(linear[0]))
728        half_height = self._radius * float(np.linalg.norm(linear[1]))
729        x1, y1 = x - half_width, y - half_height
730        x2, y2 = x + half_width, y + half_height
731        self._b_box = BoundingBox((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
732
733        return self._b_box
734
735    @property
736    def closed(self) -> bool:
737        """Return True. Circles are closed.
738
739        Returns:
740            bool: True
741        """
742        return True
743
744    @closed.setter
745    def closed(self, value: bool) -> None:
746        """No-op setter; circles are always closed."""
747
748    @property
749    def center(self) -> PointType:
750        """Return the center of the circle.
751
752        Returns:
753            PointType: The center of the circle.
754        """
755        return self.vertices[0]
756
757    @center.setter
758    def center(self, value: PointType) -> None:
759        """Set the center of the circle.
760
761        Args:
762            value (PointType): The new center of the circle.
763        """
764        self[0] = value[:2]
765
766    @property
767    def radius(self) -> float:
768        """Return the radius of the circle.
769
770        Returns:
771            float: The radius of the circle.
772        """
773        scale_x = np.linalg.norm(
774            self.xform_matrix[0, :2]
775        )  # only x scale is used
776        return self._radius * scale_x
777
778    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
779        """Check if the circle is equal to another circle.
780
781        Args:
782            other (Circle): The other circle to compare to.
783
784        Returns:
785            bool: True if the circles are equal, False otherwise.
786        """
787        if not isinstance(other, Circle):
788            return False
789        return self.id == other.id

def arc_points( center: Sequence[float], radius_x: float, radius_y: float | None = None, start_angle: float = 0, span_angle: float | None = None, end_angle: float | None = None, clockwise: bool = False, n: int = 20) -> list[Sequence[float]]: 
 955@alias_argument({"radius_x": ["radius", "r", "rx"], "radius_y": "ry"})
 956def arc_points(
 957    center: PointType,
 958    radius_x: float,
 959    radius_y: float | None = None,
 960    start_angle: float = 0,
 961    span_angle: float | None = None,
 962    end_angle: float | None = None,
 963    clockwise: bool = False,
 964    n: int = 20,
 965) -> list[PointType]:
 966    """Return a list of points that form a circular or elliptic arc.
 967
 968    Args:
 969        center: The center point of the arc.
 970        radius_x: Semi-axis along x.
 971        radius_y: Semi-axis along y; defaults to ``radius_x``.
 972        start_angle: The starting angle of the arc in radians. Defaults to 0.
 973        span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise.
 974            Mutually exclusive with ``end_angle``. At least one of
 975            ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle`` is required.
 976        end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with
 977            ``span_angle``.
 978        clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
 979        n: The number of points in the arc. Defaults to 20.
 980
 981    Returns:
 982        list[PointType]: A list of points that form an arc.
 983
 984    Examples:
 985        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 986        >>> pts = sg.arc_points((0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, end_angle=sg.pi / 2, n=4)
 987        >>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in pts]
 988        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, 20.0], [20.0, 34.641016], [0.0, 40.0]]
 989        >>> pts = sg.arc_points(
 990        ...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, span_angle=sg.pi / 2, clockwise=True, n=4
 991        ... )
 992        >>> [[round(coord, 6) or 0.0 for coord in p[:2]] for p in pts]
 993        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, -20.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
 994        >>> pts = sg.arc_points((0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, span_angle=-sg.pi / 2, n=4)
 995        >>> [[round(coord, 6) or 0.0 for coord in p[:2]] for p in pts]
 996        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, -20.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
 997        >>> pts = sg.arc_points((0, 0), 40, start_angle=-sg.pi / 2, end_angle=0, n=4)
 998        >>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in pts]
 999        [[0.0, -40.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [34.641016, -20.0], [40.0, 0.0]]
1000        >>> pts = sg.arc_points(
1001        ...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, end_angle=-sg.pi / 2, clockwise=True, n=4
1002        ... )
1003        >>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in pts]
1004        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, -20.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
1005        >>> pts = sg.arc_points(
1006        ...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=-sg.pi, end_angle=-sg.pi / 2, n=4
1007        ... )
1008        >>> [[round(coord, 6) or 0.0 for coord in p[:2]] for p in pts]
1009        [[-40.0, 0.0], [-34.641016, -20.0], [-20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
1010    """
1011    if radius_y is None:
1012        radius_y = radius_x
1013    signed_span = resolve_arc_sweep(
1014        start_angle, span_angle, end_angle, clockwise
1015    )
1016    x, y = center[:2]
1017    two_pi = 2 * pi
1018    sweep = abs(signed_span)
1019    sign = -1 if signed_span < 0 else 1
1020    if n == 1:
1021        steps = 1
1022    elif sweep == two_pi:
1023        steps = n
1024    else:
1025        steps = n - 1
1026    step = sign * sweep / steps
1027    points = []
1028    for i in range(n):
1029        angle = start_angle + step * i
1030        points.append(
1031            [x + radius_x * cos(angle), y + radius_y * sin(angle)]
1032        )
1033    return points

  • center: The center point of the arc.
  • radius_x: Semi-axis along x.
  • radius_y: Semi-axis along y; defaults to radius_x.
  • start_angle: The starting angle of the arc in radians. Defaults to 0.
  • span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise. Mutually exclusive with end_angle. At least one of span_angle or end_angle is required.

1060def rectangle_points(
1061    pos: PointType = (0, 0),
1062    width: float = 100,
1063    height: float = 100,
1064    angle: float = 0,
1065) -> Sequence[PointType]:
1066    """Return four corner points of a rectangle.
1067
1068    Args:
1069        pos: Center of the rectangle. Defaults to ``(0, 0)``.
1070        width: Rectangle width. Defaults to 100.
1071        height: Rectangle height. Defaults to 100.
1072        angle: Rotation about ``pos`` in radians. Defaults to 0.
1073
1074    Returns:
1075        Sequence[PointType]: Corner points in order (not closed).
1076
1077    Examples:
1078        >>> pts = rectangle_points((0, 0), 80, 40)
1079        >>> len(pts)
1080        4
1081        >>> [round(coord, 6) for coord in pts[0][:2]]
1082        [-40.0, -20.0]
1083    """
1084    from ..geom.affine import rotate
1085
1086    x, y = pos[:2]
1087    points = []
1088    points.append([x - width / 2, y - height / 2])
1089    points.append([x + width / 2, y - height / 2])
1090    points.append([x + width / 2, y + height / 2])
1091    points.append([x - width / 2, y + height / 2])
1092    if angle != 0:
1093        points = rotate(points, angle, (x, y))
1094    return points

1097def reg_poly_points_side_length(
1098    n: int, side_len: float, pos: PointType = (0, 0), angle: float = 0
1099) -> Sequence[PointType]:
1100    """Return vertices of a regular polygon with a given side length.
1101
1102    Args:
1103        n: Number of sides.
1104        side_len: Length of each side.
1105        pos: Center of the polygon. Defaults to ``(0, 0)``.
1106        angle: Rotation angle in radians. Defaults to 0.
1107
1108    Returns:
1109        Sequence[PointType]: Vertices of the polygon (not closed; first vertex
1110        is not repeated).
1111
1112    Examples:
1113        >>> pts = reg_poly_points_side_length(4, 40, angle=pi / 2)
1114        >>> bool(abs(float(pts[0][0])) < 1e-9)
1115        True
1116    """
1117    rad = side_len_to_radius(n, side_len)
1118    sector = 2 * pi / n
1119    x, y = pos[:2]
1120    points = [
1121        [cos(sector * i) * rad + x, sin(sector * i) * rad + y] for i in range(n)
1122    ]
1123
1124    if angle != 0:
1125        points = homogenize(points) @ rotation_matrix(angle)
1126        points = [(px, py) for (px, py, _) in points]
1127
1128    return points

def di_star(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]], n: int) -> simetri.group.batch.Group: 
1157def di_star(points: Sequence[PointType], n: int) -> Group:
1158    """Return a dihedral star with n petals.
1159
1160    Args:
1161        points (Sequence[PointType]): List of [x, y] points.
1162        n (int): Number of petals.

def hex_grid_centers( x: float, y: float, side_length: float, n_rows: int, n_cols: int) -> list[Sequence[float]]: 
1176def hex_grid_centers(
1177    x: float,
1178    y: float,
1179    side_length: float,
1180    n_rows: int,
1181    n_cols: int,
1182) -> list[PointType]:
1183    """Return a list of points that define the centers of hexagons in a grid.
1184
1185    Args:
1186        x (float): The x-coordinate of the starting point.
1187        y (float): The y-coordinate of the starting point.
1188        side_length (float): The length of each side of the hexagons.
1189        n_rows (int): The number of rows in the grid.
1190        n_cols (int): The number of columns in the grid.
1191
1192    Returns:
1193        list[PointType]: A list of points that define the centers of the hexagons.
1194
1195    Examples:
1196        >>> hex_grid_centers(0, 0, 40, 1, 1)
1197        [(0, 0)]
1198    """
1199    centers = []
1200    for row in range(n_rows):
1201        for col in range(n_cols):
1202            x_ = col * 3 * side_length + x
1203            y_ = row * 2 * side_length + y
1204            if col % 2:
1205                y_ += side_length
1206            centers.append((x_, y_))
1207
1208    return centers

def rect_grid( x: float, y: float, cell_width: float, cell_height: float, n_rows: int, n_cols: int, pattern: Sequence[Sequence[bool]]) -> simetri.group.batch.Group: 
1211def rect_grid(
1212    x: float,
1213    y: float,
1214    cell_width: float,
1215    cell_height: float,
1216    n_rows: int,
1217    n_cols: int,
1218    pattern: Sequence[Sequence[bool]],
1219) -> Group:
1220    """Return a grid of rectangles with the given parameters.
1221
1222    Args:
1223        x (float): The x-coordinate of the starting point.
1224        y (float): The y-coordinate of the starting point.
1225        cell_width (float): The width of each cell in the grid.
1226        cell_height (float): The height of each cell in the grid.
1227        n_rows (int): The number of rows in the grid.
1228        n_cols (int): The number of columns in the grid.
1229        pattern (list[list[bool]]): A pattern to fill the grid.
1230
1231    Returns:
1232        Group: A Group object representing the grid.
1233
1234    Examples:
1235        >>> grid = rect_grid(0, 0, 40, 40, 1, 1, [[True]])
1236        >>> len(grid) > 1
1237        True
1238    """
1239    width = cell_width * n_cols
1240    height = cell_height * n_rows
1241    horiz_line = line_shape((x, y), (x + width, y))
1242    horiz_lines = Group(horiz_line)
1243    horiz_lines.translate(0, cell_height, reps=n_rows)
1244    vert_line = line_shape((x, y), (x, y + height))
1245    vert_lines = Group(vert_line)
1246    vert_lines.translate(cell_width, 0, reps=n_cols)
1247    grid = Group([horiz_lines, vert_lines])
1248    for row in range(n_rows):
1249        for col in range(n_cols):
1250            if pattern[row][col]:
1251                x_, y_ = (
1252                    col * cell_width + x,
1253                    (n_rows - row - 1) * cell_height + y,
1254                )
1255                points = [
1256                    (x_, y_),
1257                    (x_ + cell_width, y_),
1258                    (x_ + cell_width, y_ + cell_height),
1259                    (x_, y_ + cell_height),
1260                ]
1261                cell = Shape(points, closed=True, fill_color=colors.gray)
1262                grid.append(cell)
1263    return grid

Return a grid of rectangles with the given parameters.

Arguments:
  • x (float): The x-coordinate of the starting point.
  • y (float): The y-coordinate of the starting point.
  • cell_width (float): The width of each cell in the grid.
  • cell_height (float): The height of each cell in the grid.
  • n_rows (int): The number of rows in the grid.
  • n_cols (int): The number of columns in the grid.
  • pattern (list[list[bool]]): A pattern to fill the grid.
Returns:

Group: A Group object representing the grid.

Examples:
>>> grid = rect_grid(0, 0, 40, 40, 1, 1, [[True]])
>>> len(grid) > 1
True
def reg_star_polygon( n: int, step: int, rad: float, **kwargs: object) -> simetri.shapes.shape.Shape | simetri.group.batch.Group: 
1266def reg_star_polygon(
1267    n: int, step: int, rad: float, **kwargs: object
1268) -> Shape | Group:
1269    """Return a regular star polygon.
1270
1271    Args:
1272        n: Number of vertices on the generating regular ``n``-gon.
1273        step: Step size for connecting vertices (star polygon parameter).
1274        rad: Circumradius of the generating regular polygon.
1275        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments passed to ``Shape``.
1276
1277    Returns:
1278        ``Shape`` or ``Group``: A single star polygon, or a ``Group`` of rotated
1279        copies when ``gcd(n, step) > 1``.
1280
1281    Examples:
1282        >>> star = reg_star_polygon(5, 2, 40)
1283        >>> star.subtype.name
1284        'SHAPE'
1285    """
1286    angle = 2 * pi / n
1287    points = [(cos(angle * i) * rad, sin(angle * i) * rad) for i in range(n)]
1288    if n % step:
1289        indices = [i % n for i in list(range(0, (n + 1) * step, step))]
1290    else:
1291        indices = [
1292            i % n for i in list(range(0, ((n // step) + 1) * step, step))
1293        ]
1294    vertices = [points[ind] for ind in indices]
1295    reps = gcd(n, step) - 1
1296    shape = Shape(vertices, **kwargs)
1297    if reps > 1:
1298        res = Group(shape.rotate(angle, reps=reps))
1299    else:
1300        res = shape
1301
1302    return res

Return a regular star polygon.

Arguments:
  • n: Number of vertices on the generating regular n-gon.
  • step: Step size for connecting vertices (star polygon parameter).
  • rad: Circumradius of the generating regular polygon.
  • **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments passed to Shape.
Returns:

Shape or Group: A single star polygon, or a Group of rotated copies when gcd(n, step) > 1.

Examples:
>>> star = reg_star_polygon(5, 2, 40)
>>> star.subtype.name
'SHAPE'
def star_shape( points: Sequence[Sequence[float]], reps: int = 5, scale: float = 1) -> simetri.group.batch.Group: 
1305def star_shape(
1306    points: Sequence[PointType], reps: int = 5, scale: float = 1
1307) -> Group:
1308    """Return a dihedral star from a list of points.
1309
1310    Args:
1311        points (list[PointType]): The list of points that form the star.
1312        reps (int, optional): The number of repetitions. Defaults to 5.
1313        scale (float, optional): The scale factor. Defaults to 1.
1314
1315    Returns:
1316        Group: A Group object representing the star.
1317
1318    Examples:
1319        >>> star = star_shape([(40, 0), (8, 8)], reps=2, scale=2)
1320        >>> star.type.name
1321        'GROUP'
1322    """
1323    shape = Shape(points, subtype=Types.STAR)
1324    group = Group(shape)
1325    group.mirror(axis_x, reps=1)
1326    group.rotate(2 * pi / (reps), reps=reps - 1)
1327    group.scale(scale)
1328    return group

Group: A Group object representing the star.

Examples:

>>> star.type.name
'GROUP'

def arc_shape( center: Sequence[float], radius_x: float, radius_y: float | None = None, start_angle: float = 0, span_angle: float | None = None, end_angle: float | None = None, clockwise: bool = False, n: int = 20) -> simetri.shapes.shape.Shape: 
1403@alias_argument({"radius_x": ["radius", "r", "rx"], "radius_y": "ry"})
1404def arc_shape(
1405    center: PointType,
1406    radius_x: float,
1407    radius_y: float | None = None,
1408    start_angle: float = 0,
1409    span_angle: float | None = None,
1410    end_angle: float | None = None,
1411    clockwise: bool = False,
1412    n: int = 20,
1413) -> Shape:
1414    """Return a Shape of a circular or elliptic arc.
1415
1416    Args:
1417        center: The center of the arc.
1418        radius_x: Semi-axis along x.
1419        radius_y: Semi-axis along y; defaults to ``radius_x``.
1420        start_angle: The starting angle of the arc in radians. Defaults to 0.
1421        span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise.
1422            Mutually exclusive with ``end_angle``. At least one of
1423            ``span_angle`` or ``end_angle`` is required.
1424        end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with
1425            ``span_angle``.
1426        clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
1427        n: The number of points to use for the arc. Defaults to 20.
1428
1429    Returns:
1430        Shape: A Shape object with points that form an arc.
1431
1432    Examples:
1433        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1434        >>> arc = sg.arc_shape((0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, end_angle=sg.pi / 2, n=4)
1435        >>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
1436        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, 20.0], [20.0, 34.641016], [0.0, 40.0]]
1437        >>> arc = sg.arc_shape(
1438        ...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, span_angle=sg.pi / 2, clockwise=True, n=4
1439        ... )
1440        >>> [[round(coord, 6) or 0.0 for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
1441        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, -20.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
1442        >>> arc = sg.arc_shape((0, 0), 40, start_angle=-sg.pi / 2, end_angle=0, n=4)
1443        >>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
1444        [[0.0, -40.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [34.641016, -20.0], [40.0, 0.0]]
1445        >>> arc = sg.arc_shape(
1446        ...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, end_angle=-sg.pi / 2, clockwise=True, n=4
1447        ... )
1448        >>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
1449        [[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, -20.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
1450        >>> arc = sg.arc_shape(
1451        ...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=-sg.pi, end_angle=-sg.pi / 2, n=4
1452        ... )
1453        >>> [[round(coord, 6) or 0.0 for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
1454        [[-40.0, 0.0], [-34.641016, -20.0], [-20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
1455    """
1456    points = arc_points(
1457        center,
1458        radius_x,
1459        radius_y,
1460        start_angle=start_angle,
1461        span_angle=span_angle,
1462        end_angle=end_angle,
1463        clockwise=clockwise,
1464        n=n,
1465    )
1466    return Shape(points, closed=False, subtype=Types.ARC)

Return a Shape of a circular or elliptic arc.

Arguments:
  • center: The center of the arc.
  • radius_x: Semi-axis along x.
  • radius_y: Semi-axis along y; defaults to radius_x.
  • start_angle: The starting angle of the arc in radians. Defaults to 0.
  • span_angle: Sweep in radians. A negative value draws clockwise. Mutually exclusive with end_angle. At least one of span_angle or end_angle is required.
  • end_angle: Ending angle in radians. Mutually exclusive with span_angle.
  • clockwise: If True, the arc is drawn clockwise. Defaults to False.
  • n: The number of points to use for the arc. Defaults to 20.

>>> import simetri.graphics as sg

>>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
[[0.0, -40.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [34.641016, -20.0], [40.0, 0.0]]
>>> arc = sg.arc_shape(
...     (0, 0), 40, start_angle=0, end_angle=-sg.pi / 2, clockwise=True, n=4
... )
>>> [[round(coord, 6) for coord in p[:2]] for p in arc.vertices]
[[40.0, 0.0], [34.641016, -20.0], [20.0, -34.641016], [0.0, -40.0]]
>>> arc = sg.arc_shape(

def inflate( item: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, offset: float) -> simetri.shapes.shape.Shape: 
1626def inflate(item: Shape, offset: float) -> Shape:
1627    """Return a copy of ``item`` grown or shrunk by ``offset``.
1628
1629    Positive ``offset`` expands every side (or the radius of a circle).
1630    Negative ``offset`` deflates. The result has the same type as ``item``.
1631    ``item`` is not mutated.
1632
1633    Args:
1634        item: A ``Square``, ``Rectangle``, ``Circle``, ``Ellipse``, or closed
1635            ``Shape``.
1636        offset: Distance added to each side, or to a circle's radius.
1637
1638    Returns:
1639        Shape: A new object of the same type as ``item``.
1640
1641    Raises:
1642        TypeError: If ``item`` is not a supported shape type.
1643        ValueError: If ``item`` is an open or degenerate ``Shape``, or if the
1644            result would have a non-positive size.
1645
1646    Examples:
1647        >>> sq = square(40)
1648        >>> out = inflate(sq, 20)
1649        >>> type(out).__name__
1650        'Square'
1651        >>> out.width
1652        80.0
1653        >>> sq.width
1654        40.0
1655        >>> float(inflate(sg.Circle(20), 20).radius)
1656        40.0
1657        >>> inflate(Rectangle(80, 80), -20).width
1658        40.0
1659        >>> inflate(Ellipse(80, 40), 20).width
1660        120.0
1661        >>> poly = sg.Shape([(-20, -20), (20, -20), (20, 20), (-20, 20)], closed=True)
1662        >>> [float(round(coord, 6)) for coord in inflate(poly, 20).vertices[0][:2]]
1663        [-40.0, -40.0]
1664    """
1665    if not isinstance(item, Shape):
1666        raise TypeError(f"inflate does not support {type(item).__name__}")
1667
1668    inflated = item.copy()
1669    if isinstance(item, Circle):
1670        new_radius = inflated.radius + offset
1671        if new_radius <= 0:
1672            raise ValueError("inflate would make radius non-positive")
1673        inflated.radius = new_radius
1674        return inflated
1675    if isinstance(item, Ellipse):
1676        new_width = inflated.width + 2 * offset
1677        new_height = inflated.height + 2 * offset
1678        if new_width <= 0:
1679            raise ValueError("inflate would make width non-positive")
1680        if new_height <= 0:
1681            raise ValueError("inflate would make height non-positive")
1682        center = inflated.center
1683        _, rotation, _ = decompose_transformations(inflated.xform_matrix)
1684        vertices = [
1685            tuple(point)
1686            for point in ellipse_points(
1687                center, new_width / 2, new_height / 2, rotation
1688            )
1689        ]
1690        inflated[:] = vertices
1691        inflated.a = new_width / 2
1692        inflated.b = new_height / 2
1693        return inflated
1694    if isinstance(item, Square):
1695        new_size = inflated.width + 2 * offset
1696        if new_size <= 0:
1697            raise ValueError("inflate would make size non-positive")
1698        inflated.scale(new_size / inflated.width, about=inflated.center, reps=0)
1699        return inflated
1700    if isinstance(item, Rectangle):
1701        new_width = inflated.width + 2 * offset
1702        new_height = inflated.height + 2 * offset
1703        if new_width <= 0:
1704            raise ValueError("inflate would make width non-positive")
1705        if new_height <= 0:
1706            raise ValueError("inflate would make height non-positive")
1707        center = inflated.center
1708        x0, y0 = inflated.vertices[0][:2]
1709        x1, y1 = inflated.vertices[1][:2]
1710        angle = atan2(y1 - y0, x1 - x0)
1711        x, y = center[:2]
1712        half_width = new_width / 2
1713        half_height = new_height / 2
1714        vertices = [
1715            (x - half_width, y - half_height),
1716            (x + half_width, y - half_height),
1717            (x + half_width, y + half_height),
1718            (x - half_width, y + half_height),
1719        ]
1720        if angle != 0:
1721            vertices = (
1722                homogenize(vertices) @ rotation_matrix(angle, center)
1723            ).tolist()
1724        inflated[:] = vertices
1725        return inflated
1726    if not inflated.closed:
1727        raise ValueError("inflate requires a closed Shape")
1728    if len(inflated) < 3:
1729        raise ValueError("inflate requires a Shape with at least 3 vertices")
1730    vertices = list(offset_polygon(inflated.vertices, offset))
1731    if len(vertices) >= 2 and close_points_square(vertices[0], vertices[-1]):
1732        vertices = vertices[:-1]
1733    xs = [point[0] for point in vertices]
1734    ys = [point[1] for point in vertices]
1735    if max(xs) - min(xs) <= 0 or max(ys) - min(ys) <= 0:
1736        raise ValueError("inflate would make size non-positive")
1737    inflated[:] = vertices
1738    return inflated

Return a copy of item grown or shrunk by offset.

Positive offset expands every side (or the radius of a circle). Negative offset deflates. The result has the same type as item. item is not mutated.

Arguments:
  • item: A Square, Rectangle, Circle, Ellipse, or closed Shape.
  • offset: Distance added to each side, or to a circle's radius.
Returns:

Shape: A new object of the same type as item.

Raises:
  • TypeError: If item is not a supported shape type.
  • ValueError: If item is an open or degenerate Shape, or if the result would have a non-positive size.
Examples:
>>> sq = square(40)
>>> out = inflate(sq, 20)
>>> type(out).__name__
'Square'
>>> out.width
80.0
>>> sq.width
40.0
>>> float(inflate(sg.Circle(20), 20).radius)
40.0
>>> inflate(Rectangle(80, 80), -20).width
40.0
>>> inflate(Ellipse(80, 40), 20).width
120.0
>>> poly = sg.Shape([(-20, -20), (20, -20), (20, 20), (-20, 20)], closed=True)
>>> [float(round(coord, 6)) for coord in inflate(poly, 20).vertices[0][:2]]
[-40.0, -40.0]
def offset_polygon_shape( polygon_shape: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, offset: float = 1, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> simetri.shapes.shape.Shape: 
1741def offset_polygon_shape(
1742    polygon_shape: Shape,
1743    offset: float = 1,
1744    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1745) -> Shape:
1746    """Return a polygon ``Shape`` with offset edges.
1747
1748    Args:
1749        polygon_shape: Source polygon ``Shape``.
1750        offset: Offset distance (positive expands outward). Defaults to 1.
1751        abs_tol: Distance tolerance for offset construction. Defaults to
1752            ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1753
1754    Returns:
1755        Shape: A new closed polygon with offset vertices.
1756
1757    Examples:
1758        >>> src = square(size=40)
1759        >>> out = offset_polygon_shape(src, offset=2)
1760        >>> out is not src
1761        True
1762        >>> [float(round(coord, 6)) for coord in out.vertices[0][:2]]
1763        [-22.0, -22.0]
1764    """
1765    if abs_tol is None:
1766        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1767    vertices = offset_polygon(polygon_shape.vertices, offset, abs_tol)

def snap( free_shape: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, ref1: float, fixed_shape: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, ref2: float, angle: float = 0) -> simetri.shapes.shape.Shape: 
1772def snap(
1773    free_shape: Shape,
1774    ref1: float,
1775    fixed_shape: Shape,
1776    ref2: float,
1777    angle: float = 0,
1778) -> Shape:
1779    """Snap ``free_shape`` to ``fixed_shape`` at the given references.
1780
1781    References are vertex indices (``int``) or barycentric edge coordinates
1782    (``float``). For closed polygons, vertex walks are assumed counter-clockwise.
1783
1784    When ``angle`` is zero, edges meeting at the snap points align edge-to-edge.
1785    Otherwise ``free_shape`` is rotated about the coincident point so the angle
1786    between the adjacent edges matches ``angle``.
1787
1788    Integer ``ref``: snap at vertex ``k``.
1789    Float ``ref``: snap at a point on an edge; for example ``1.5`` is the
1790    midpoint of the edge from vertex 1 to vertex 2 (zero-based indexing).
1791
1792    Args:
1793        free_shape (mutated): Shape moved and rotated into place.
1794        ref1: Reference on ``free_shape`` (vertex index or edge coordinate).
1795        fixed_shape: Shape that stays fixed.
1796        ref2: Reference on ``fixed_shape``.
1797        angle: Target angle in radians between adjacent edges at the snap point.
1798            Defaults to 0 (edge-to-edge alignment).
1799
1800    Returns:
1801        The transformed ``free_shape`` (same object, mutated in place).
1802
1803    Examples:
1804        >>> free = square(center=(0, 0), size=80)
1805        >>> fixed = square(center=(40, 0), size=80)
1806        >>> snapped = snap(free, 1, fixed, 0)
1807        >>> snapped is free
1808        True
1809        >>> bool(abs(float(snapped[1][0]) - float(fixed[0][0])) < 1e-9)
1810        True
1811    """
1812
1813    def get_edge_indices(shape: Shape, ref: float) -> tuple[int, int]:
1814        """Get the edge indices for alignment.
1815
1816        For a vertex index, returns (prev_vertex, vertex).
1817        For a barycentric coordinate, returns the two vertices of the edge.
1818
1819        Args:
1820            shape: The shape
1821            ref: The reference (int or float)
1822
1823        Returns:
1824            Tuple of (previous_index, current_index)
1825
1826        Raises:
1827            ValueError: If ref is at a boundary of a non-closed shape
1828        """
1829        n_vertices = len(shape.vertices)
1830        is_closed = shape.closed
1831
1832        if isinstance(ref, int):
1833            # For vertex: need vertices at ref-1, ref, ref+1
1834            if not is_closed:
1835                if ref == 0:
1836                    raise ValueError(
1837                        "Cannot snap at first vertex (index 0) of a non-closed shape"
1838                    )
1839                if ref >= n_vertices - 1:
1840                    raise ValueError(
1841                        f"Cannot snap at last vertex (index {ref}) of a non-closed shape"
1842                    )
1843            prev_idx = (ref - 1) % n_vertices if is_closed else ref - 1
1844            return (prev_idx, ref)
1845        elif isinstance(ref, float):
1846            # For edge point: need vertices at edge_index, edge_index+1, edge_index+2
1847            edge_index = int(ref)
1848            if not is_closed and edge_index >= n_vertices - 2:
1849                raise ValueError(
1850                    f"Cannot snap at edge {edge_index} of a non-closed shape with {n_vertices} vertices"
1851                )
1852            next_index = (
1853                (edge_index + 1) % n_vertices if is_closed else edge_index + 1
1854            )
1855            return (edge_index, next_index)
1856
1857    free = free_shape
1858    fixed = fixed_shape
1859    # Get the reference points on both shapes
1860    ref1_point = free[ref1]
1861    ref2_point = fixed[ref2]
1862
1863    # Move the free object to make ref1 and ref2 coincident
1864    dx = ref2_point[0] - ref1_point[0]
1865    dy = ref2_point[1] - ref1_point[1]
1866    free.translate(dx, dy)
1867
1868    # Update ref1_point after translation
1869    ref1_point = ref2_point
1870
1871    # Get edge information for angle calculation and rotation
1872    # Get edge indices for alignment
1873    _, free_curr_idx = get_edge_indices(free, ref1)
1874    fixed_prev_idx, _ = get_edge_indices(fixed, ref2)
1875
1876    # Get the direction vectors for angle calculation
1877    # For edge points (float): use the edge direction
1878    # For vertices (int): use incoming and outgoing edges
1879
1880    # For the fixed shape (incoming direction to snap point)
1881    fixed_prev = fixed[fixed_prev_idx]
1882
1883    # For the free shape (outgoing direction from snap point)
1884    free_next = free[free_curr_idx]
1885
1886    # Calculate the current angle between the edges
1887    # The angle is measured from the fixed edge (incoming) to the free edge (outgoing) at ref1_point
1888    current_angle = angle_between_lines3(fixed_prev, ref1_point, free_next)
1889
1890    # Calculate rotation needed to achieve the desired angle
1891    rotation_needed = angle - current_angle
1892
1893    # Rotate the free object around ref1_point by the computed angle
1894    free.rotate(rotation_needed, about=ref1_point)
1895
1896    return free

Snap free_shape to fixed_shape at the given references.

References are vertex indices (int) or barycentric edge coordinates (float). For closed polygons, vertex walks are assumed counter-clockwise.

When angle is zero, edges meeting at the snap points align edge-to-edge. Otherwise free_shape is rotated about the coincident point so the angle between the adjacent edges matches angle.

Integer ref: snap at vertex k. Float ref: snap at a point on an edge; for example 1.5 is the midpoint of the edge from vertex 1 to vertex 2 (zero-based indexing).

Arguments:
  • free_shape (mutated): Shape moved and rotated into place.
  • ref1: Reference on free_shape (vertex index or edge coordinate).
  • fixed_shape: Shape that stays fixed.
  • ref2: Reference on fixed_shape.
  • angle: Target angle in radians between adjacent edges at the snap point. Defaults to 0 (edge-to-edge alignment).
Returns:

The transformed free_shape (same object, mutated in place).

Examples:
>>> free = square(center=(0, 0), size=80)
>>> fixed = square(center=(40, 0), size=80)
>>> snapped = snap(free, 1, fixed, 0)
>>> snapped is free
True
>>> bool(abs(float(snapped[1][0]) - float(fixed[0][0])) < 1e-9)
True
def fillet_shape_corners( shape: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, d_vert_radius: dict[int, float], n: int = 12) -> simetri.shapes.shape.Shape: 
1899def fillet_shape_corners(
1900    shape: Shape, d_vert_radius: dict[int, float], n: int = 12
1901) -> Shape:
1902    """Return a copy of ``shape`` with rounded corners.
1903
1904    Args:
1905        shape: Source polygon or polyline.
1906        d_vert_radius: Mapping ``vertex_index -> fillet radius`` for corners to round.
1907        n: Number of points per fillet arc. Defaults to 12.
1908
1909    Returns:
1910        A copy of ``shape`` with fillet vertices substituted.
1911
1912    Examples:
1913        >>> src = square(size=40)
1914        >>> rounded = fillet_shape_corners(src, {0: 1}, n=4)
1915        >>> rounded is not src
1916        True
1917        >>> len(rounded.vertices) > len(src.vertices)
1918        True
1919    """
1920    vertices = fillet_corners(shape.vertices, d_vert_radius, n)
1921
1922    new_shape = shape.copy()
1923    new_shape[:] = vertices
1924
1925    return new_shape
